title: The best of the AI trade could be behind us. Here’s how to prepare, according to Barclays.
key_facts: Investing.com, 16 Oct: Barclays strategist Emmanuel Cau said hot inflation data, renewed Middle East tensions and a chip-stock sell-off are testing the bank's 'narrow path higher' thesis for equities.
In his note Cau wrote that the AI theme is entering 'a more mature phase' with valuations, funding needs, competition, regulation and revenue visibility under greater scrutiny.
He wrote that 'it is certainly conceivable that the best of the AI thematic trade may be behind us'.

The SOX chip index and KOSPI lost about 8% and 14% this week; Cau cited memory-chip competition, funding and valuation worries after two Asian data-centre firms delayed IPOs, and scrutiny of AI capital spending.

He attributed much of the weakness to positioning rather than a meaningful deterioration in fundamentals, citing strong demand guidance from ASML and TSMC, and said Big Tech fundamentals remain generally supportive.
Barclays continues to favour a balanced sector allocation and sees Europe as a diversifier.
